subject: High p95 after model-kappa v2c deploy — next steps / unpin request
messages:
From: Eric Jansen <eric.jansen@novusbank.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: ops@novusbank.com
Date: 2026-09-12T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: model-kappa v2c deploy impacting p95 — urgent

Marcus,

We started seeing a sharp jump in p95 latency right after your v2c roll earlier this morning. Our internal dashboards show p95 moving from ~280ms to ~1.2s across a subset of endpoints that hit the chat completions path. The spike correlates with your deploy at 07:40 PT. This is causing timeouts on our UI and some user-facing errors.

Can you pin traffic back to the previous stable variant immediately or rollback the deploy? We need the service behavior restored to prior latency within the hour.

I can share screenshots and logs — attaching a snapshot.

Thanks,
Eric Jansen
Director, Platform Engineering
Novus Bank
[attachment: latency-dash.png (image/png)]

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: Eric Jansen <eric.jansen@novusbank.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-12T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: model-kappa v2c deploy impacting p95 — urgent

Eric — thanks for flagging and for the dashboard. We’ve opened INC-9876 in our infra queue and I’ve put an immediate traffic pin on the live variant so requests are routing to model-kappa v2b (the previously stable variant). That should short-circuit most of the customer impact while we triage.

Quick status:
- Traffic pinned to v2b at 08:18 PT.
- Infra has a perf snapshot and initial heap/CPU traces are being collected.
- We see a reproducible p95 increase for sequences with long system prompts — looks like a path that triggers an attention kernel fallback.

Before we do a full rollback to the code that produced v2b, product recommends considering a rollforward patch (v2d) that contains a kernel fix and correctness guards. Rollback could reintroduce a separate correctness regression we saw two weeks ago.

As the Novus contact, do you want us to: 1) keep the pin and run a canary of v2d at 10% traffic, or 2) perform a full rollback to v2b? We can start the canary immediately but it requires authorization for a short SLA exception window so the canary may briefly show elevated p95 while we validate.

I’ll coordinate legal and CS once you confirm.

—Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Cc: infra-oncall@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-12T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: model-kappa v2c deploy impacting p95 — urgent

Folks — quick engineering assessment:
- Root cause: v2c introduced a fallback into a slower attention kernel when a small set of request shapes hit the large-context path. The fallback is functionally correct but ~3–4x slower at p95.
- Risk analysis: a full rollback to v2b will recover latency immediately but will re-enable an earlier edge-case correctness issue (reported in INC-9711) that affected a small percentage of requests. That correctness issue caused subtle hallucinations for one enterprise customer last month.

Recommended path (lower customer/brand risk):
1) Keep traffic pinned to v2b for remediation timing.
2) Launch a controlled rollforward to v2d (contains a targeted kernel patch + guardrails) as a 10% canary for 30 minutes, monitor p95, error rates, and a small set of correctness evals.
3) If canary metrics look good (p95 back near baseline, no regression in correctness eval), increment to 50% then 100% over 2–3 hours.

Attachments: canary-plan.md (validation checks, metrics thresholds), perf-snapshot.csv (baseline vs v2c).

I’m requesting authorization for: a) temporary SLA carveout for the 30–90 minute canary window (metrics may transiently show elevated p95), and b) permission to notify legal to prepare a short amendment for the live service-level terms and potential one-off credit if Novus requests it.

If approved I’ll trigger the canary and have infra watch the telemetry dashboards.

—Hannah Schmitt
Product Manager, Serving Runtime
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
[attachment: canary-plan.md (text/markdown)]
[attachment: perf-snapshot.csv (text/csv)]

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: legal@redwood.com, cust-succ@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-12T12:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: model-kappa v2c deploy impacting p95 — next steps / unpin request

Thanks for the quick work and the clear assessment. Naomi here — I approve the canary rollforward path to v2d with the following constraints:
- Canary at 10% for 30 minutes, observability watch (infra + PM) required.
- If p95 during canary > 600ms or correctness eval failures > 0.1% relative to baseline, abort and return to pinned v2b.
- Offer Novus Bank a one-time service credit (0.5% of monthly committed spend) proactively; CS should draft the message.
- Legal: please prepare a short amendment/ack that covers the temporary SLA carveout and the operational rollback gate. HubSpot deal: HS-654321 — please attach amendment.

Marcus, notify Novus and start the canary once infra confirms deploy readiness. Keep the thread updated with live metric links.

—Naomi Feldman
VP, Customer Success & Sales Operations
naomi_feldman@redwood.com
